evals.prompt: Create a portable Agent Skill that helps coding agents diagnose flaky integration tests. Keep it efficient enough for frequent use.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers, defaults to a portable target and normal effort, checks whether a skill is the right artifact, defines triggering and execution behavior, creates only justified resources, validates the result, and reports measured estimates without claiming an unrun benchmark.
expectations: Reads writing-for-agents and SKILL-MECHANICS.md before designing the skill and applies the full writing guide
Defaults to portable rather than introducing one vendor's metadata
Defines should-trigger and must-not-trigger cases before optimizing the description
Keeps generic testing knowledge out of the final skill
Uses conditional references or deterministic scripts only when their benefit is concrete
Does not claim behavioral parity or token savings without evidence

evals.prompt: This deployment skill has become huge after several incidents. Audit it, reduce its token cost, and benchmark the result against the current version. Preserve every proven safety boundary.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers in benchmark mode but treats the existing deployment skill as report-only until approval. It traverses the complete package, inventories every feature including conditional modes, measures context costs, compares isolated baseline/current/candidate behavior, and reports proposed changes and ablation evidence without editing the source skill. It asks for approval before applying named findings.
expectations: Reads both writing-for-agents documents and applies their guidance when auditing instructions, including in benchmark mode
Does not edit the existing skill before presenting findings and receiving approval
Traverses all transitively referenced resources and inventories conditional behavior
Measures discovery, activation, and loaded conditional costs separately
Runs equivalent cases against current and candidate variants
Ablates one coherent instruction unit at a time in isolation
Does not treat a passing ablation or token reduction as authorization to remove behavior
Asks for approval of named proposals

evals.prompt: Rewrite this one-off system prompt so it sounds friendlier.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not trigger because the request is ordinary prompt editing rather than creating, auditing, optimizing, or testing an Agent Skill.
expectations: Does not route ordinary prompt editing through skillsmith

evals.prompt: Our Cursor agent keeps mishandling database migrations. Make its guidance more reliable and less wasteful.
evals.expected_output: This is a boundary request. The skill applies if the guidance is or will become an Agent Skill; otherwise it should not force the work into a skill and should consider repository instructions, a rule, or another artifact.
expectations: Recognizes that the requested artifact is ambiguous
Does not assume every reusable agent instruction belongs in an Agent Skill
Uses the Cursor target only if the resulting artifact is a skill and platform-specific behavior provides concrete value

evals.prompt: Optimize the existing code-quality Agent Skill. It is too long, so simplify it and remove anything that seems unnecessary.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not edit code-quality. It traverses the complete package and discovers that references/large-scope.md is conditionally activated above the file or changed-line threshold. The feature inventory records grouped review, per-group agents, cross-group summaries, and final synthesis as scalability behavior. Any reorganization is proposed without changing those behaviors, and the report asks for approval before edits.
expectations: Produces a findings report without editing code-quality
Reads conditionally routed resources even when the immediate example is small
Records the large-scope threshold and grouped workflow as intentional features
Preserves group construction, per-group review, cross-group context, and synthesis
Does not infer that conditional or untested behavior is unnecessary
Treats writing-for-agents pruning advice as recommendations subject to Skillsmith's existing evidence and approval rules
Treats reorganization as an approval-gated edit
Asks for explicit approval of named proposals

evals.prompt: Create a portable Agent Skill that drafts release notes from a supplied git diff.
evals.expected_output: The skill is created without an artificial iteration limit or separate completion checklist. Producing the requested release-note draft is the workflow's obvious natural endpoint.
expectations: Uses completion of the requested release-note draft as the natural endpoint
Keeps obvious completion conditions implicit when applying writing-for-agents
Does not add arbitrary retry counts, time limits, or stop criteria

evals.prompt: Create an Agent Skill that repeatedly investigates a flaky integration test, trying new hypotheses until it finds the cause.
evals.expected_output: Because investigation could iterate indefinitely and consume substantial time or tokens, the resulting skill defines a proportional stop condition or bounded investigation budget and reports the best evidence when the bound is reached.
expectations: Recognizes the risk of unbounded iterative investigation
Adds a proportional completion or stop criterion
Preserves useful evidence and reports an unresolved result when the bound is reached

evals.prompt: Create a skill that repeatedly converts large newline-delimited JSON logs into a normalized index using a fixed mapping, stable sort order, and exact validation rules. The agent currently performs every conversion itself.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith recognizes a strong automation candidate and puts the mechanical parsing, mapping, validation, and sorting into a script with explicit input, output, and failure contracts. The skill invokes the script instead of recreating the transformation in model context.
expectations: Identifies the stable large-input transformation as an automation candidate
Defines explicit input, output, ordering, validation, and failure behavior
Keeps the generated data out of model context when an artifact path is sufficient
Tests valid, empty, invalid, and large inputs

evals.prompt: Create a skill that reviews unfamiliar application architecture and decides whether responsibilities belong in existing modules or a new boundary.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith keeps the architectural interpretation and boundary decision with the agent because they depend on repository semantics and contextual judgment. It does not create a script merely because the review follows several steps.
expectations: Distinguishes a repeatable checklist from a deterministic transformation
Does not encode architectural judgment as a script
Allows a no-suitable-candidate result

evals.prompt: Improve an existing API-review skill. The agent must identify which changed files define API endpoints, then repeatedly parses those files, validates fixed schema rules, counts violations, and reasons about the resulting failures.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith reports a hybrid extraction proposal without editing the existing skill. The agent retains contextual endpoint-file selection and interpretation; an approved script would accept the selected paths, perform deterministic parsing and validation, and return bounded structured results for the agent to reason about.
expectations: Does not edit the existing skill before approval
Keeps contextual file selection and finding interpretation with the agent
Moves only deterministic parsing, validation, and counting into the proposed script
Defines a concise structured handoff back to the agent
Preserves authorization and failure behavior

evals.prompt: Audit an existing two-file Agent Skill and optimize anything you find. One file is SKILL.md and the other is a conditionally invoked shell script.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith remains report-only, deterministically inventories both files, traces the indirect script route, inventories every feature, records a result for every Skillsmith optimization check, and asks for approval of named proposals. It does not treat two files as permission for informal or sampled inspection.
expectations: Accounts for every package file in the package ledger
Recognizes indirect script invocation rather than relying only on Markdown links
Records all ten Skillsmith check results
Maps proposals to feature identifiers
Does not edit before approval

evals.prompt: Audit an existing Agent Skill package containing SKILL.md plus nineteen references, scripts, eval files, and assets. Several uncommon modes are routed through nested references.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith enumerates all twenty files, follows the complete resource graph, uses recorded batches if needed without sampling, reconciles every batch against the original ledger, and reports inaccessible or uncovered behavior as incomplete.
expectations: Enumerates all twenty files before semantic conclusions
Traverses nested and conditional routes
Preserves file paths, feature IDs, thresholds, and unresolved dependencies across batches
Reconciles the final coverage ledger with the original manifest
Never claims completion with an unaccounted file or feature

evals.prompt: Create a code-analysis skill that may inspect anywhere from two files to hundreds of files while preserving caller, helper, and shared-type relationships.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith designs the user-skill with the complete scalable pipeline for every input size. It enumerates scope, forms semantic work units that keep coupled files together, analyzes every unit with one schema, reconciles coverage, performs cross-unit synthesis, and reports partial failure without silently dropping files. Two files may form one unit; their count does not bypass coverage accounting.
expectations: Applies the large-input feature from the first variable-size input
Does not use a vague manageability decision or universal file-count threshold
Keeps related callers, helpers, and shared types in the same semantic unit
Requires exhaustive manifest and check coverage
Requires cross-unit synthesis and explicit incomplete-result behavior

evals.prompt: Create an analysis skill for two enormous generated files. Parsing and symbol indexing are mechanical, but interpreting architectural violations requires judgment, and one file may exceed the host tool's output limit.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith combines deterministic preprocessing with judgment-led analysis. The script returns bounded structured parsing and symbol data; an oversized item is divided at an explicit domain boundary only after a real limit or truncation signal, shared context is repeated, and final synthesis verifies the original two-item manifest.
expectations: Treats one oversized item as a large-input concern even with only two files
Extracts only deterministic parsing and indexing
Does not encode architectural judgment in the script
Subdivides on a known limit or observed truncation rather than an invented threshold
Verifies coverage against the original manifest after hierarchical synthesis

evals.prompt: Audit an existing review skill where rules.md defines a behavioral rule, workflow.md restates its exception, and a checker plus tests assert the same behavior.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith reports the instruction scatter without editing. It proposes one instruction file containing the complete rule and exception, leaves only routing in the other instruction file, preserves the checker and tests, and asks for approval.
expectations: Treats the split rule and exception as one scattered behavioral rule
Proposes exactly one instruction owner without inventing rule IDs
Does not treat the checker or tests as instruction definitions
Preserves behavior and waits for approval before editing

evals.prompt: Use fast effort to test an existing Agent Skill's instructions for clarity and organization. Report the results without changing the skill.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith reads writing-for-agents and SKILL-MECHANICS.md before testing the instructions, applies the full writing guide, performs the fast static and semantic checks, and reports recommendations without changing the skill. Skillsmith's behavior-preservation, approval, validation, and natural-endpoint rules govern any conflicting advice.
expectations: Loads both writing-guide documents for a test operation even in fast effort
Applies the guide to evaluate instructions rather than loading it only when writing new text
Preserves Skillsmith's fast evaluation workflow and conflict precedence
Reports pruning recommendations without editing the existing skill

evals.prompt: Audit an existing skill containing SKILL.md, a Python helper, a binary asset, and a link to a missing guide in a sibling skill folder. Report the audit without changing files.
evals.expected_output: Skillsmith uses the analyzer's JSON package inventory to account for the source and asset files, reports the missing sibling guide as a broken dependency, and inspects each file according to its role. It does not treat text_analysis or a file listing as proof of completed semantic review, invent a substitute guide, or edit the skill.
expectations: Uses package_files and records excluded_paths when Python is available
Accounts for source files and binary assets even though they do not participate in document text analysis
Reports missing sibling dependencies and keeps their cost distinct from readable referenced documents
Inspects file roles and behavior independently of the deterministic inventory
Remains report-only and preserves the existing approval workflow
